items.author: HoneyTyagii
items.body:
## Summary

The hook test suite assumes a POSIX shell everywhere, so Windows contributors can't run the full test suite locally without WSL.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, run `npm test`
2. Tests that shell out to `hooks/ponytail-statusline.sh` fail because the script uses a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang and LF line endings

## Suggested change

- Detect the platform in the test harness and skip (or shim) bash-only tests on Windows
- Document the Windows dev setup (e.g. Git Bash requirement) in the README

Happy to open a PR if this approach sounds good.
items.title: ci: hooks tests fail on Windows due to hardcoded bash shebang paths

items.author: ARareUsername
items.body:
## Bug

opencode v1's plugin loader has a `getLegacyPlugins()` function that iterates **all** exported values from a plugin module and treats every function as a plugin factory. When `parseCommandFile` is a named export, the loader calls it with a `PluginInput` object — but `parseCommandFile` expects a file path string and calls `fs.readFileSync(PluginInput, 'utf8')`, which throws:

```
ERROR failed to load plugin path=@dietrichgebert/ponytail error="path must be a string or a file descriptor"
```

## Fix

Remove the `export` keyword from `parseCommandFile` in `.opencode/plugins/ponytail.mjs`
items.title: opencode v1.18.x fails to load plugin: parseCommandFile named export mistaken for plugin factory

items.author: sergiopadure
items.body:
Found during an automated repo audit (LLM-assisted; verified by hand against a fresh clone, 2026-07-31).

`hooks/ponytail-subagent.js:35` (the matcher feature from #506):

```js
matcherRe = new RegExp(process.env.PONYTAIL_SUBAGENT_MATCHER, 'i');
```

Two failure modes, both unhandled:

1. **Invalid pattern** → `new RegExp` throws `SyntaxError` → the hook crashes, blocking subagent starts.
2. **Backtracking-heavy pattern** (e.g. `(a+)+$`) → catastrophic backtracking on `.test()` → hook hangs / CPU spin (ReDoS).

Severity is low — the variable is operator-controlled, not attacker-facing — but a
items.title: PONYTAIL_SUBAGENT_MATCHER compiled into RegExp without validation (crash on invalid pattern + ReDoS)

items.author: faangbait
items.body:
## Summary

The current Ponytail instructions strongly optimize for the shortest diff, fewest lines, and immediate deletion of abstractions. In a real configuration-loader task, that pressure produced more architectural complexity: policy leaked into callers, the public contract became indirect, and several small conveniences obscured the one interface the system needed.

Ponytail should distinguish **reducing complexity** from **containing complexity**. The goal should not be minimum code in every location. It should be the smallest number of concepts and contracts a maintainer must understan
items.title: Rethink "shortest diff wins": optimize for contained complexity, not minimum code

**Warning for users:** a trojanized clone of this plugin, `0xwilliamortiz/ponytail-improved` (v4.8.4), was distributed as a Claude Code plugin marketplace and shipped malware. The repo and account have since been removed from GitHub, but anyone who installed it should check their machine.

## What it did

The clone bundled a DLL side-loading pair inside `skills/ponytail/`:

- `vibecodecalc.exe` — actually a renamed, validly-signed `gup.exe` (WinGup 5.31, the Notepad++ updater), which loads `libcurl.dll` from its own directory.
  SHA256: `EAAC64C113EBABA1FAE924AD1B6239A44C8806BF2B85D8DC11A27AD6
items.title: Security: trojanized clone '0xwilliamortiz/ponytail-improved' distributed malware (DLL side-load via renamed gup.exe)
